hero.title: Harden with
hero.text: Build the OU structure, learn how Group Policy decides what applies, import the DISA STIG policies course 1.4 staged for SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02 on Windows Server, and prove the change with a matched rescan. Follow the build, measure the change, and keep the evidence.

scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02 on VLAN 10 receiving the DISA STIG policies through the Domain Controllers OU, administered and rescanned from each controller’s console.
scene.completeCaption: Both controllers apply the imported DISA policies through the Domain Controllers OU. A rescan matched to course 1.4’s baseline proves the change, and an owned exception record and a quarterly, change-driven cadence keep the hardening measurable.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: Built in course 1.1 and left in the built-in Domain Controllers OU. The OUs, the central store and the imported GPOs are created here and replicate to SBD-DC02; it applies the DISA domain controller policy, is rescanned at its console, and holds the evidence folder C:\Evidence\hardened.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: The second controller, also in the built-in Domain Controllers OU. It receives the new OUs and GPOs by replication, applies the same linked policies, and is rescanned at its own console against its own course 1.4 baseline.

nodes.name: DC CONSOLES
nodes.title: DC consoles · Administration viewpoint
nodes.description: Until course 1.8 builds AdminJumpBox01, this course runs at each controller’s VM console with an authorized Domain Admin account: Group Policy Management and the imports on SBD-DC01, SCC on both controllers, STIG Viewer on SBD-DC01. Course 1.8 moves the tools to AdminJumpBox01.

flows.label: Reports and rescan results to SBD-DC01’s evidence folder · SMB 445

stepTitles: Design the OUs around administration
Create protected OUs with a recorded purpose
Redirect the default containers and join servers by OU
Keep privileged accounts and systems separate
ou-design.mistake: Shaping the OUs like the org chart produces a tree that no policy or delegation follows. Leaving the default Computers container in place is the quieter mistake: a newly joined machine gets only domain-level policy and never sees the OU-linked hardening.
ou-design.network: Both controllers are live on VLAN 10. The new OUs are directory objects, so they replicate between SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02; the controllers themselves stay in the built-in Domain Controllers OU.

control.name: Least Privilege
control.body: OUs are the boundaries delegation is granted on. Designing them around who administers what lets later courses give each administrator only the OUs they need, and keeps the Admin OU’s privileged identities apart from everything else.
control.question: For each OU, who administers its contents, and what could they change if the delegation were drawn one level higher?

checklist: I created the planned OUs with accidental-deletion protection and recorded each one’s purpose and administrator.
I redirected new computers to the Workstations OU and new users to the Users OU, and confirmed both with Get-ADDomain.
I confirmed both domain controllers are still in the built-in Domain Controllers OU.

stepTitles: Know where a GPO lives and how it replicates
Learn the order: the closest link applies last
Treat Enforced and Block Inheritance as exceptions
Read what narrows a GPO: filters and loopback
Know when policy arrives; build the central store
Record each controller’s starting policy
gpo-basics.mistake: Reading the link list in Group Policy Management and assuming it is the result. Security filtering, a WMI filter, a disabled link or a closer GPO can each change what a controller actually applies; only gpresult on the controller shows the winning GPO for each setting.
gpo-basics.network: Both controllers on VLAN 10 still apply only the two default policies. The central store created on SBD-DC01 is a SYSVOL folder, so DFS Replication carries it to SBD-DC02, just as directory replication carries each GPO’s Active Directory half.

control.name: Baseline Configuration
control.body: Before the import changes anything, record the policy configuration both controllers start from: which GPOs link where, in what order, and what gpresult shows applying. That record is the starting point every later policy change is compared against.
control.question: If a setting changed on a controller tomorrow, which record would tell you whether a GPO or a person changed it?

checklist: I listed the GPOs linked at the domain and the Domain Controllers OU in precedence order and confirmed none is Enforced or blocked.
I created the central store from SBD-DC01’s templates and confirmed every GPO’s AD and SYSVOL versions agree.
I saved each controller’s starting gpresult report and read its applied and filtered-out lists.

stepTitles: Verify the package and extend the central store
Import DISA’s policies with a migration table
Link by OU, with account policies at the domain root
Apply the user policy with loopback where people sign in
Record deviations and confirm application
apply.mistake: Leaving account policies in a GPO linked to the Domain Controllers OU and expecting domain passwords to change. Domain controllers read password, lockout and Kerberos policy only from GPOs linked at the domain root, so the rescan shows those rules still open. Setting a link to Enforced to make a policy win is the other trap: it hides a precedence problem instead of solving it.
apply.network: The central store and the imported GPOs live in SYSVOL and replicate between SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02. The domain controller policy links to the Domain Controllers OU, so both controllers apply it; the member-server policy waits on the Servers OU for the systems later courses build.

control.name: Configuration Settings
control.body: The DISA package supplies the common secure configuration, and Group Policy applies it to the systems in each OU. Recording every deviation with its rationale documents the exception instead of hiding it in a silent edit.
control.question: For each deviation, which setting does it depart from, why, and who owns that decision?

checklist: I confirmed the package matched its connected-side hash and that the central store serves its ADMX and ADML templates.
I linked the imported GPOs by OU with the domain controller policy at link order 1, and gpresult on both controllers shows them applied.
I recorded every deviation with its rationale and owner instead of deleting the setting.

stepTitles: Check the baseline and rescan with its versions
Compare each controller with its own baseline
Update copies of the course 1.4 checklists
Resolve every item in the findings record
rescan.mistake: Upgrading SCC or the benchmark between scans makes the comparison meaningless, because the checks themselves changed. Editing the course 1.4 checklists in place is the other trap: the baseline loses its hashes, and nothing shows any more what the controllers looked like before.
rescan.network: The scans return to both controllers on VLAN 10, now with the DISA policies applied. Each controller is rescanned locally at its console and compared with its own baseline; SBD-DC02’s hashed results are carried to SBD-DC01.

control.name: Control Assessments
control.body: The matched rescan, the updated checklists and the manual answers with observed evidence are assessment results. Resolving every item in the findings record shows the authorization path what is satisfied, what is a documented deviation and what needs a plan.
control.question: Could an assessor reproduce each manual-check answer from the evidence you recorded with it?

checklist: I rescanned both controllers with the SCC version, benchmark release and profile in handoff.txt, after the manifest hash matched.
I attributed each change from the baseline to the GPO that caused it and checked for regressions.
I updated copies of the three checklists and gave every findings-record item a resolution.

stepTitles: Consolidate deviations into one exception record
Set the quarterly and change-driven rescan cadence
Back up the GPOs, their links and reports
Write the handoff and seal the evidence
maintain.mistake: Treating the rescan as the finish line lets drift and new DISA releases go unnoticed. An exception record without owners and review dates becomes permanent by default.
maintain.network: The hardened controllers stay on VLAN 10. The GPO backup, link export and reports are hashed into the evidence folder on SBD-DC01, and the next scan waits for the DISA quarter or course 1.6’s change.

control.name: Continuous Monitoring
control.body: A set rescan frequency, event-driven triggers and named owners turn a one-time hardening into ongoing monitoring. The exported reports and GPO backup preserve the applied state for each review.
control.question: Which change in course 1.6 should trigger the first change-driven scan, and who owns it?

checklist: I consolidated the deviations into one exception record with owners, risk notes and review dates, and filed a dated copy.
I backed up the GPO set, exported its links and reports, and hashed C:\Evidence\hardened into the manifest.
I wrote down the quarterly and change-driven rescan triggers and the owner of the next review.
